notes:
HEADCOUNTS. Most site figures are the "annual average number of employees" for calendar year 2025 that each establishment reported to OSHA on Form 300A (file: ITA_300A_Summary_Data_2025_through_08-31-2026.csv, linked from https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data). I read every such figure in the file itself; each employeesNote names the establishment row. It is a government source about that one site and that year, but it is self-reported, covers the whole establishment (offices on the same site included) and can include supervised temporary workers. Where a company statement about the site was found and read, it is used instead and the OSHA figure is given in the note (Samsung Austin 3,342 vs OSHA 5,016; Samsung Taylor 1,150 vs 767; SkyWater about 1,000 vs 881). Not from OSHA: Schneider El Paso (company expectation for end of 2023, all El Paso plants together), Wistron (Nvidia statement, July 2026), Celestica (expansion announcement, June 2026), Mission Solar (company testimony). No site figure, left null: Tower Semiconductor San Antonio (a January 2022 San Antonio Express-News report of 660 workers could not be opened), Leonardo DRS Dallas, Powell Mosley Road and Jacintoport, LS Electric Bastrop (a local paper reports 50 hires in its first phase), Tesla Megafactory. stateEmployees is null throughout: no source stating a Texas manufacturing total was read. SUBSECTOR CALLS, each following the NAICS code the plant reports rather than the grouping in the brief: (1) Applied Materials Austin is 333242, so Machinery Manufacturing. (2) Encore Wire, Prysmian and Southwire report 331420 (copper wire drawing), so Primary Metal Manufacturing; a reviewer who wants wire and cable under Electrical Equipment should change the subsector on those four plants (and null the NAICS). (3) Solar panel plants (Canadian Solar, T1 Energy, Waaree, Mission Solar) are 334413, so Computer and Electronic Product Manufacturing, not Electrical Equipment; T1 itself filed 333414, which I did not follow. STATUS CALLS. TI's older Sherman fab (150 mm) is marked closed on the strength of reports that the line was wound down at the end of 2025; its coordinates are from EPA's facility registry and are less certain than the others. Mission Solar is marked closed because the company said in 2026 that manufacturing had "temporarily ceased"; it may restart. Samsung Taylor is "under construction" (the company said the fab would be operational by the end of 2026; not confirmed). COMPANIES THAT MAY ALSO BE IN OTHER BRIEFS: Tesla (only the Megafactory is listed here; Giga Texas is a vehicle plant), SpaceX (only the Bastrop Starlink plant), Raytheon, Abbott, Siemens, Eaton, Flex. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. Dell: no current manufacturing in Texas was found (the Austin PC plant closed in 2008). Infineon: its Austin fab is now SkyWater's Fab 25; the existing database may list that plant under Infineon, Cypress Semiconductor or Spansion, which are not given as other names because they are different companies. L3Harris (Greenville 4,798, Waco 1,400 in the OSHA file) and Lockheed Martin Missiles and Fire Control (Grand Prairie 3,901, Lufkin 485) report aircraft and missile NAICS codes and belong to the transportation equipment brief.
